body:
Refs #1448. Follow-up of #3334.

## What happens

Waterjet Profile is on `main` now. It does not take a start pick or an exit pick. `KindInfo::pick()` answers `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` for `OpType::WaterjetProfile` (`crates/app/src/operation/pick_kinds.rs`). A pick on a waterjet operation is refused by name. The user cannot set the pierce point or the place where the jet goes off.

#3334 gave the rule for this kind: "A waterjet kind that `main` adds later takes the same pick through the shared mechanism." The plasma slice of #3334 did not include the waterjet planner.

## Expected

- Start: the pierce is at the lead-in start that lands on the projection of the start pick on the profile.
- Exit: the lead-out and the jet off are at the projection of the exit pick.
- The picks are the operation-level `picks` (#3339). MCP `edit_operation` sets them.

Seam: `crates/motion/src/waterjet/plan.rs` (the seam is `longest_mid`). The plasma slice is the pattern: `crates/motion/src/plasma/picks.rs` (`assign`, `run_on`) and `plan_closed` in `crates/motion/src/plasma/emit.rs`. The pick assignment can move to `crates/motion/src/sheet/` so that the two kinds share it.

## Laws a pick must keep (refused by name, never moved)

- The pierce is in the scrap, not on the part that stays.
- The lead room and the kerf compensation hold at the pick.
- The tabs keep their laws (`crates/motion/src/waterjet/tabs.rs`): a pick does not move or remove a tab.

## Done means

- A pin test shows the pierce at the start pick and the jet off at the exit pick, with golden CL.
- A pin test shows a pick whose pierce falls on the part refused by name.
- Undo and redo restore the previous path. MCP `edit_operation` sets the picks.
- Each shipped waterjet golden without a pick is byte-identical.

Safety floor: this changes toolpaths and posted G-code.

Priority note: a follow-up found during work is `P7` by the Issue Law. The other issues of the start and exit series have `P2`. The maintainer decides if this one moves up.

## What

The catalog case `3d/rough-finish` runs near its 60 s budget in the debug suite `app:example_catalog`. It fails on the budget when the machine is loaded.

The two tests are `catalog_3d_rough_finish::rebuilds` and `catalog_3d_rough_finish::regenerates`. The budget is in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/support.rs` (the line `did not finish within ... move this case to app heavy: example_catalog or reduce its model`).

## Evidence

Measured on a 6-core Windows machine (i7-8700T), debug test binary, command `catalog_3d_rough_finish` with the six tests of that module in one process. Main is `d94b9816d`. The head is PR #3965 at `d94b3f7e8`. The PR does not touch the 3D path.

| Case | Load | Main `regenerates` / `rebuilds` | PR head `regenerates` / `rebuilds` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 runs | idle | 28.7-28.9 s / 29.2-29.4 s | 28.8-29.1 s / 29.2-29.4 s |
| 3 runs | 6 busy loops on 6 cores | 56.0, 60.0 (FAIL), 56.1 s / 46.3, 40.6, 43.1 s | 56.7, 39.6, 39.9 s / 41.6, 59.4, 59.3 s |

- On main, run 2 under load failed: `3d/rough-finish regenerates: did not finish within 60s`.
- On the PR head, two runs under load ended at 59.3 s and 59.4 s, which is 0.6 s from the limit.
- On the review machine of #3965 (16 jobs) the cases took 23.4 s and 23.0 s on main and 21.8 s and 19.2 s on the head. The first run on the head failed on the 60 s limit and the retry passed.

Earlier sightings of the same budget failure:
- #3458, at a load average of about 130: `rebuilds` passed the limit by 0.11 s.
- #3163 (open): the same failure for the case `2d/adaptive-pocket`.

## Done means

One of these, decided by the maintainer:
- the case moves to the heavy lane (as the message says);
- the case gets a smaller model;
- the case gets a budget with margin, for example 2 times its idle time.

The cases then finish with a clear margin under load in debug.

What happens: the analytic wire contour of #3937 (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/arc_cut.rs`, `stitch`) joins two arcs whose snapped ends differ by a few nanometres with a connector line. The post rounds that line to the coordinates of the arc end, so the program has a `G1` block with no motion after the arc.

Evidence: the golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_dxf_spline_die.nc` of PR #3958 has 74 `G3` blocks and 72 zero-length `G1` blocks. A DXF SPLINE or ELLIPSE (#1865) is read as tangent arcs, so each joint of such a chain is an arc-arc joint.

Expected: two tangent arcs follow each other with no connector block. The program is about half as long.

Why it matters: the blocks are safe (the laws check each move), but they double the program length of each curve, and some controls warn on a block with no motion.

Done means: a spline die posts with no `G1` block between two arcs, the kerf and cover laws still pass, and the margin note still covers the nanometre offsets. The goldens of #3937 stay byte-identical, or the PR names each one that moves.

title: Tool meridian of a sharp taper or a drill misses the radial shoulder when the flute is shorter than the cone

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

`Tool::meridian()` (`crates/tools/src/meridian.rs`) and `Tool::profile()` disagree for a sharp tapered mill or a drill when the flute length is shorter than the cone. The profile steps out to the full radius at the flute top. The meridian does not add that radial shoulder, so it ends at a smaller radius.

The review of PR #3929 found this class for flat and ball taper tips (review comment 7144791597). PR #3929 fixes it for the new flat and ball tips only (`crates/tools/src/taper.rs`, `meridian_points`). It does not change sharp tapers or drills, because that PR keeps their output byte-identical. The same missing shoulder stays on `main` for sharp tapers and drills.

## Why it matters

The two shapes describe the same tool. If code reads the meridian for a collision, gouge, simulation or solid, it sees a smaller tool than the profile and the real cutter. That can hide a contact. The filer has not traced each reader of the meridian; this needs a check before the priority is set.

## What to check

- Each reader of the tool meridian for milling tools (sim tool bodies, solids, fidelity checks, stamps).
- A sharp taper and a drill with a flute shorter than the cone: compare `profile()` and `meridian()` at the flute top. A test in the style of `taper::tests::short_flat_profile_and_meridian_agree` (PR #3929) shows the gap.

## Done means

For every tool kind, the meridian and the profile agree at the flute top, including the radial shoulder of a short flute. A test pins a sharp taper and a drill with a short flute. Any changed digest or golden is listed in the PR.

The account that files this issue cannot set labels. A collaborator: please set the priority (P1 if a collision or gouge check reads the meridian, else P3), `bug`, an effort label, the area label and `source:agent`.

Found while fixing #3929.

body:
## What happens

A Wire EDM contour on a DXF chain that contains an arc or a circle fails to generate. The maintainer reported it.

```
generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: Wire Contour1: invalid machining parameters: the selected DXF chain contains an arc or circle; the generic wire path requires straight segments
```

The refusal is made at `crates/app/src/operation/wire_sketch.rs:247`.

## Why it matters

A circle and an arc are the most common wire EDM shapes: a punch, a die opening, a hole. The generic wire path cannot cut either one. This blocks the basic use of the wire feature. The maintainer set the priority at `P1`.

## What is expected

- The wire path accepts an arc and a circle from the DXF chain.
- The path is cut as an arc: a wire machine interpolates an arc from its own block (G02/G03 with I/J or R), so the toolpath and the post carry the arc, not a long chord list.
- A full circle without a lead-in point has a start rule (a lead-in on the circle, or a slit), and the path says which.

## Related issues

- #3215: "Wire output writes no arcs: circles and fillets become G01 chords". The output side of the same class. This issue is the generation side.
- #3216: Wire Contour closing overlap, centre-line slit cutting, skims on open contours.
- #2702: G-EDM XYUV taper and 4-axis ruled wire post support.
- #2692: XYUV wire EDM swallowtail test fixtures.
- #2871: Example case: Wire Contour, and a taper that the machine refuses.

## What to check

- The refusal at `wire_sketch.rs:247`: which chain kinds reach it, and whether the generic path has an arc arm at all.
- The wire post vocabulary: a dialect that writes an arc block (G02/G03 with I/J) and the one that accepts only G01.
- The pin `crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection.rs:219` asserts the refusal. It changes when the feature lands.

## Missing at filing

- The DXF and the operation parameters. Add them as a comment when the case is reproduced.

title: 2D Contour outside, several parts at one level: the rings after the first plunge through the pass link, with no note

body:
## What happens

An outside 2D Contour with entry Ramp or Helix enters its first ring by the entry. PR #3833 ramps the first ring of each level on the wall side.

Each ring after the first ring at the same level is reached through the pass link. `contour_link::ring_link` lifts, crosses and plunges straight down at the plunge feed. The posted program has an axial dive at each of these rings. No note says so.

This is the same fault as #3830 on the bore side. PR #3834 fixes the bore side only.

## Reading

Setup: no compensation, tool diameter 6 mm, stepdown 1 mm, 3 levels, bottom Z -3, ramp angle 5 degrees. Each part is a 16 mm square. The parts are 40 mm apart. Counts are plunge moves / axial dives, measured on a branch that has #3833.

| Entry | 1 part | 2 separate parts | 3 separate parts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ramp 5 degrees | 0 / 0 | 3 / 3 | 6 / 6 |
| Plunge | 3 / 3 | 6 / 6 | 9 / 9 |

Ramp and Helix post no note about these dives. Helix posts only its stand-down note.

## Where

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs`: `ring_to_ring`, then `ring_link`. The bore side asks for the entry. The wall side does not.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_link.rs`: `ring_link`, the lines after the keep-down proof (`guard`, then `MoveKind::Plunge`).

## Expected

One of these:
- Each ring after the first ring takes the entry (ramp or helix), by the wall-side ramp of #3833.
- Or the generator names the plunge in a note, as the bore side does for the tabbed case.

The compensation refusal of #3890 stays: control and wear compensation refuse Ramp and Helix on both sides.

## Done means

- A test with n separate parts and entry Ramp shows no axial dive and no plunge move. It fails on main.
- The traverse between the parts rides the pass link plane (the rule of review item 1 on #3834).

Refs #3829, #3830.

title: UI link on Windows: the CLI does not check that the window on a stale port is the real window

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found in a security review of PR #3861 (part 1 of #3751).

**What happens**

On Windows the link is TCP on 127.0.0.1 with a port that the OS selects (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:221-226`). The discovery file `<pid>.json` holds the port and the token (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:44-57`). A window that crashes does not remove its file (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:159-168` runs only on a normal drop). Only a new window with the same pid replaces it.

The CLI connects to each candidate file (`crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:165-174`):

- `crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:101-137`: `open` sends the token, then accepts any peer that answers `HELLO_OK`. The window does not prove that it knows the token.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:133-135`: after the hello, there is no read deadline.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:207-210` and `:249`: `read_line` and `io::copy` read the answer with no size limit.

A different local user can bind the stale port on 127.0.0.1. That user then gets the stale token and the arguments of each tool call (for example file paths). That user can also send false tool results to the CLI, or a line with no end that makes the CLI use all memory. That user cannot run commands in a real window.

On Unix this risk does not occur: the folder is mode 0700 (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:196-204`).

**Expected**

The CLI talks only to the real window. Possible fixes:

- The window proves that it knows the token (for example an answer that includes a hash of the token and a client nonce).
- Before it connects, the CLI checks that the pid in the file is alive, and it removes a stale file.
- The CLI reads each answer line with a size limit.
- Alternative: a named pipe with a user-only ACL replaces the TCP port (the decision in `docs/decisions/3751-cli-ui-link.md` names this option).

**Done means**

- The CLI refuses a peer that does not prove the token.
- The CLI reads answers with a size limit.
- A test in `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs` starts a false server on a stale entry and shows that the CLI sends no tool call to it.

Refs #3751, PR #3861.

title: UI link: a client without the token can hold the only link session for 5 minutes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found in a security review of PR #3861 (part 1 of #3751).

**What happens**

The UI link serves one client at a time. The token check is on the first line, but the same deadlines apply before and after the token check:

- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:181`: the link uses `IDLE_TIMEOUT` (5 minutes) for its listener.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:233-255`: `accept_loop` serves clients one after the other.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:283-351`: before the hello line, the read loop accepts up to `MAX_LINE` (16 MiB, line 56) and waits up to the idle window.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:330-334`: the token check occurs only when a complete line arrives.

On Windows the link is TCP on 127.0.0.1 (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:221-226`). Each local user can connect to that port. A client without the token can connect and send no newline. It then holds the only session for 5 minutes. It can connect again after the drop. During that time, `camcraft-cli --ui` cannot reach the window. The app also buffers up to 16 MiB for an unauthenticated client.

No command runs, and the UI thread does not stop. This is a denial of service of the link only.

**Expected**

A client that does not send a valid hello line in a short time (for example 5 s) is closed. The hello line has a small size limit (for example 4 KiB). The 5-minute idle window and the 16 MiB limit apply only after the token check.

**Done means**

- A pre-hello deadline and a pre-hello size limit exist in `listen.rs`.
- A test in `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs` connects, sends no hello, and shows that a second client with the token gets a session after the short deadline.

Refs #3751, PR #3861.

body:
## Problem

The 2D Offset rings merge at concave places where two lobes join. At such merges, corner movements by more than one stepover cause some cuts to take the full tool width without a name.

Readings on `testdata/models/fig8.step`:

| Pass starts at | full-width cut points (`flanks::full_width_points`) |
|---|---|
| Outside (one ring set, #3744) | 495, all at the waist band, Y 40 to 70 |
| Inside (the same ring set) | 10686 (most are first ring along part wall, which is named) |
| Outside before #3744 (rings parallel to stock box) | 0 |

The full-width cuts at the waist are not named. `level_order::full_width_at` measures distance to nearest cut (1.9 tool radii). The ring arms near merge are inside that distance, so "narrow" note does not come. This is a load issue, not a gouge.

## Why P1

AGENTS.md, Prime Directive: a result that is not safe must be refused or the toolpath must give a visible diagnostic. Unnamed full-width cuts can cause cutter overload without warning.

## Fix

- Ring merges should not take full tool width, or they are named on the path.
- Option 1: Use `full_width_at` metric (like flanks meter) to detect ring merge points where steps exceed one stepover distance and emit a "full-width" note.
- Option 2: Apply Held's rule for offset curve merges - smaller local step between ring corners more than one stepover apart.

## Pins

- `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width`: #3744 moved its reading from 0 to "at most 520 points, all in waist band". The fix sets it back to 0.
- A motion pin on a synthetic two-lobe part that reads full-width points at the merge, for Inside and Outside.

Done means: the two pins are green, and no unnamed full-width cut is left at a ring merge.

## Notes

- Related: #3743, #3744.
- This issue was found during fixing of #3744 (one ring set for Auto, Inside and Outside).

body:
Found by the reporter in v0.26.0 via the AI Chat panel (2026-11-23). Reproduced headlessly with the 0.26.0 `camcraft-cli`; the same code is on `main`.

## What happens

On a mounted Tormach 770MX (ML) (`spindle_max` 10000 rpm), `add_tool { "catalog": "EM-0300-2FL" }` and `add_tool { "catalog": "EM-0400-2FL" }` copy the catalog's 15000 and 12000 rpm into the document as they are. Nothing says they are above the machine: the `add_tool` reply carries only the holder note, `add_operation` and `generate` add no note, and the first word of it is the machine check at verify / post, which holds the program:

```
machine Tormach 770MX (ML): 2 limit problem(s): 2D Adaptive1: tool EM-0300-2FL runs 15000 rpm, above the machine's 10000; 2D Contour1: tool EM-0400-2FL runs 12000 rpm, above the machine's 10000
```

The block itself is right (the Prime Directive holds: no over-limit S word is posted). The defect is that it comes last, after the work is generated, and that the other paths that set a speed already hold it to the machine and say so:

- `apply_cutting_data` / `suggest_cutting_data` (`crates/app/src/cutting.rs`, `compute`): "45094 rpm held to the machine's 10000".
- the Feeds tab spindle row (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/spindle_row.rs`, `hold_to_machine`): "spindle speed N rpm held to the machine's maximum M".

Only adding a catalog tool (MCP `add_tool`, `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs` `add_tool` -> `AddTool::with_holder`) takes the catalog rpm with no reading of the mounted machine. The verify problem also does not say what to do about it (edit the tool's speed, or `apply_cutting_data`).

## Steps to reproduce

`simple.step` is a 25.4 x 25.4 x 1.27 mm plate. Script `b.js`, run with `camcraft-cli script b.js`:

```js
cam.import("simple.step", "simple");
cam.call("load_machine", {builtin: "Tormach 770MX (ML)"});
cam.call("set_stock", {box: {dx: 37.4, dy: 37.4, dz: 5.27}});
cam.log(JSON.stringify(cam.call("add_tool", {catalog: "EM-0300-2FL"})));   // no rpm word
cam.log(JSON.stringify(cam.call("add_tool", {catalog: "EM-0400-2FL"})));   // no rpm word
cam.call("add_operation", {kind: "2D Adaptive", tool: "EM-0300-2FL", source: "stock"});
cam.call("add_operation", {kind: "2D Contour", tool: "EM-0400-2FL", source: "simple"});
cam.generate();                       // generates, no rpm note
cam.log(JSON.stringify(cam.verify())); // gate ok:false, the problem above
```

## Expected

When a tool is added (MCP `add_tool`, and the UI's add from the catalog) while a machine with a `spindle_max` (or `spindle_min`) is mounted and the tool's rpm is outside it, the reply / status says so at once, e.g. `"warning": "EM-0300-2FL runs 15000 rpm, above the Tormach 770MX (ML)'s 10000 - the post will be held; set the tool's speed (edit_tool) or apply_cutting_data"`. The machine check at verify keeps blocking as now, and its problem line names the same fix. The tool's rpm is not changed silently by the add (a library speed stays what the user stated; the warning tells them).

## Where

- `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs` `add_tool` (the reply has `note` for the holder only).
- `crates/app/src/commands/tool.rs` `AddTool` (where a note like the holder note can be built from the mounted machine).
- `crates/post/src/machine/check.rs` and `crates/app/src/posting_default_machine.rs`: the "runs N rpm, above the machine's M" problem text, which could name the fix.

Found while fixing #3744 (one ring set for Auto, Inside and Outside). Related: #3743.

## What happens

The one ring set of #3744 is the offsets of the part. At a concave place of the part, the offsets of two lobes merge. At the merge, the corner of each ring moves by more than one stepover from the corner of the next ring. Thus some cuts there take the full tool width.

Readings on `testdata/models/fig8.step` (the `offset_pass_start` heavy fixture: EM-0800-4FL, stock margin 5 mm, Outside containment):

| Pass starts at | full-width cut points (`flanks::full_width_points`) |
|---|---|

| Inside (the same ring set) | 10686 (most are the first ring along the part wall, which is named) |
| Outside before #3744 (rings parallel to the stock box) | 0 |

- The full-width cuts at the waist are not named. `level_order::full_width_at` measures the distance to the nearest cut (1.9 tool radii). The ring arms near the merge are inside that distance, so the "narrow" note does not come.
- This is a load issue, not a gouge. The gouge and crossing checks are clean on this pass.

## Expected

- The rings at a merge do not take the full tool width. One option: clean-up rings or a smaller local step between two ring corners that are more than one stepover apart (Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", 1991, covers the merge of offset curves).
- A cut that still takes the full width is named on the path, by the same law that the flanks meter uses.

## Pins

- `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width` (heavy): #3744 moved its reading from 0 to the bound "at most 520 points, all in the waist band". The fix sets it back to 0.
- A motion pin on a synthetic two-lobe part that reads the full-width points at the merge, for Inside and Outside.

Part of #3743. Builds on step 1 (#3750). Step 5 of the migration.

## The maintainer's words

#3741: "Where it should have just followed the contour keeping its plan not lifting the tool."

#3741 rule: "Each ring goes around the part in the plane of the cut and stays at depth. The tool does not lift between the parts of one ring."

## What happens

Circular has its own ring code: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs:233-340` (`rho = rc - stepover * k` at `:289`, the Inside order at `:288`, the rim helix at `:300`). It walks each ring as its own ladder (`run_level_walks` for each ring, `:340`). Each call makes a new `WalkState` with `first: true` (`levels.rs:328-329`). Thus each ring enters again from the clearance height, and each entry goes down into material. The rings are not linked at depth.

## Fix approach

1. Circular gets its rings from `ring_set` with the circle input. The rings stay exact G2/G3 circles at the same radii.
2. One walk for each level over all rings. The link from ring k to ring k+1 is a stepover link at depth by `ring_links` (a radial line or a tangent arc in the cut plane).
3. One entry for each level by `ring_entry`. The rim helix stays as the entry where the tool must enter material.
4. A lift needs a named reason.

## Pins

- `circular_rings_link_at_depth`: a circular pocket with 4 rings has one entry and 0 lifts on each level.
- `circular_rings_unchanged`: the ring radii and the arc count of each ring are the same as on the head before this change.

#3741: "Where it should have just followed the contour keeping its plan not lifting the tool."

#3741 rule: "A lift is permitted only when an in-plane link would cut the part or a fixture. Then the status line names the reason."

## What happens

2D Pocket uses the same start-side planner as 2D Offset, with the dead-end ramps on (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs:314-318`, `ring_plan_ramped(..., true)`). Thus a Pocket with Pass starts at Inside or Outside has the defects of #3741: other rings for each start side, a lift at each piece, and the #3577 dead-end ramps.

Pocket Waterline and OffsetRings use a second planner (`waterscan.rs:62-216`, through `pocket_plan.rs:20-36`). Its rings are chained only where a chord is clear (`waterscan.rs:217`). Each other pass break lifts by the `Retract` pass link of `Links::PLANAR` (`crates/motion/src/links.rs:86-94`, `ladder_links.rs:163`), with no proof and no reason.

## Fix approach

1. 2D Pocket gets its rings from `ring_set` with `RingRef::Boundary` (the walls and the islands, Held 1991). Waterline, OffsetRings, Inside and Outside all use it. Pass starts at changes only the order of k and the start point.
2. The links between rings use `ring_links`. A lift has a named reason.
3. The entry uses `ring_entry`. A closed pocket has no air path, so the first entry is a pre-drilled hole, a cleared column, or the user's helix or ramp. A pocket that is open to the stock edge enters in air.
4. Remove the Pocket call of `ring_plan_ramped` and of `plan_passes` for the ring strategies.

## Pins

- `pocket_inside_and_outside_cut_the_same_rings`: on a square pocket with a round island, Inside, Outside and Waterline give the same multiset of rings (1 um, after a start-point and direction normalisation).

body:
## Request

The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-23. His words: "Make the camcraft-cli able to interact witht he ui. By adding the flag --ui, so it instead sends it commands directly to the UI and changes gets reflected in the UI. This allows for alot better interaction and end2end testing, for dealing with UI improvements and for endusers also doing setups. The CLI improvements should come with a --skill <folder,claude,copiplot> install creating a AI skill for working with the CLI tool."

The maintainer set the priority P2.

## Part 1: `camcraft-cli --ui`

- With `--ui`, the CLI does not run the commands in its own headless world. It sends them to a running CamCraft UI.
- The UI runs each command through the same undoable command history as the GUI ("Everything Is a Command"). The change shows in the UI at once, and Ctrl+Z undoes it.
- The CLI prints the result of each command and returns a non-zero exit code on an error, as in headless mode.
- When no UI is running, the CLI gives a clear error. It does not fall back to headless mode silently.
- Uses: end-to-end tests of UI changes, agent-driven checks of the UI, and set-up of a project by a user from a script.

Questions to decide (record each in `docs/decisions/`):
1. The transport: a local socket or a named pipe. Find the UI with a discovery file in the user's data folder. Bind only to the local machine.
2. Security: accept only local connections from the same user. Use a token in the discovery file. Never listen on a network port.
3. The protocol: reuse the MCP tool surface (`crates/app/src/mcp/`) so that the CLI, MCP and the GUI call the same commands. Do not make a second command set.
4. Several UI windows: select one by project path or process id.
5. Windows, Linux and macOS from the same source ("Stays buildable everywhere").

## Part 2: `camcraft-cli --skill <target> install`

- `<target>` is one of `folder`, `claude` or `copilot`.
- `folder`: write the skill files into a given folder.
- `claude`: install the skill where Claude Code reads skills, for the user or for the project.
- `copilot`: install it where GitHub Copilot reads custom instructions.
- The skill text comes from one source in the repository, and it lists the CLI verbs, the `--ui` mode and examples. Relate it to #1947 (single-source AI agent skills) and to the existing `camcraft-mcp` skill.
- A test checks that the installed skill names each CLI verb that exists (a drift test).

## Pins

- A UI test starts the app through the test harness, sends one command with `--ui`, and checks that the UI state changed and that undo restores it.
- A CLI test with no running UI checks the clear error and the exit code.
- A test for each `--skill` target writes into a temporary folder and checks the files.

## Notes

- This is new design (an IPC transport and a protocol), thus effort:max.
- Slices are permitted: part 1 first, then part 2.

body:
Part of #3741. Builds on #3744 (one ring set) and #3745 (the approach distance).

## The maintainer's words

"The arc atm, is showing as a "straight" plunge down.. which is fine for transporting to the plane, but it should happen outside the stock box. - and also we see no movement of a an arc to wal into the wall of the stockbox - so no viable approach is getting generated using the Arc approach. The Arc Sweep and Arc Radius inpputs does nothing to affect the approach"

About Inside: "picking "inside" makes perfect rings, but the cutter planges straight down into the material.. instead of starting outside the stock box"

## What happens

Inside and Outside share one entry path: `ladder_links.rs:55-92` (`descend`) -> `descent.rs:120-149` (`plan`) -> `descent.rs:216-286` (`plan_arm`). One fix covers the two.

1. The entry is placed at the first point of the first pass (`descent.rs:217`). For Outside that point is on the stock edge. For Inside it is at the part wall, in solid stock.
2. The `Arc` entry is a vertical-plane arc onto the first cut (`entry.rs:37-41`, `descent.rs:262-277`). Its lead chord is proved against the cutter-centre area (`descent.rs:271`). For Outside that area ends at the stock box, so the air outside the box is never legal. `entry_arc.rs:146-152` returns "the arc's lead room is blocked".
3. `descent_dive.rs:169-187` (`substituted_dive`) then posts "axial dive on the floor instead". Its fix text (helix radius, start hole) does not apply to a start side.
4. The horizontal (G17) arc entry (`arc_xy`, `descent_xy.rs:205-220`) is skipped when the arm is `Arc` (`:218-219`), and it proves only inside the legal area.

Readings (synthetic dog-bone part, 80 x 50 stock box, D8, stepover 2; see the #3741 research comment):

- Outside, Arc entry: the first dive has its tool centre 0.50 mm INSIDE the stock box. Arc radius 4 -> 10 and Arc sweep 90 -> 45 do not change the path.
- Inside, Plunge entry: 8 plunges; the first one is 8.41 mm inside the box, in solid stock.
- Same on `e313aa663` (#3353): this is not a regression of #3577.

## Fix approach

A new entry law for a start-side pass (Inside and Outside, and Auto through #3744):

1. Rapid to a point P outside the stock box. The distance from P to the box is at least the tool radius plus the approach distance (#3745).
2. Feed down in air at P to the cut Z.
3. Feed in the cut plane: an optional straight lead, then a G17 arc of Arc radius and Arc sweep, tangent onto the first ring. Arc radius and Arc sweep come from `Approach::arc_radius` / `arc_sweep`.
4. Prove the lead path against the stock box grown by the approach distance and the tool radius, not against the cutter-centre area. It must not touch the part or a fixture. Where no lead fits, refuse with a named reason. Do not post a silent plunge.
5. Outside: the first ring is at the stock edge, so the lead runs in air and enters the stock wall on the arc.
6. Inside: the first ring is at the part wall, and stock can enclose it. Recommended option (the maintainer's words): the entry still starts in air outside the box, and the in-plane lead feeds through the stock to the first ring. This feed is a slot at the full tool width, so it uses the plunge feed and the status line names it. Dropped: a helix in material for Inside (the maintainer asks for an air entry). Record the choice in `docs/decisions/`.
7. Check the Lead in / Lead out page. The maintainer saw Helix, Ramp and Plunge disabled for Outside. That page code was not found on `main` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/lead_page.rs:25-44, 89-102` show all four kinds). Make the page offer only Arc and a straight approach for Inside and Outside.

## Pins (red first, from the maintainer's comment)

- `outside_entry_plunges_in_air`: the plunge XY is outside the stock box by at least the tool radius plus the approach distance.
- `outside_first_cut_is_an_arc_in_the_plane`: the first cutting move after the plunge is a G17 arc at the cut Z.
- `arc_radius_changes_the_lead`: a change of Arc radius changes that arc's radius in the output; a change of Arc sweep changes its sweep.
- `inside_entry_is_no_plunge_into_material`: no entry of an Inside pass is a straight plunge into material (the maintainer's pin).
- `start_side_entries_have_no_helix_or_ramp`: no Inside or Outside entry is a helix or a ramp.

Effort `max`: a new entry geometry with a new legal-area proof, under the safety floor.

Done means: the five pins are green on the dog-bone part and on the committed `testdata/models/fig8.step`.

title: A .camtools library cannot hold a form-profile mill, a blunt tapered mill, or a single-form thread mill without a pitch range

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
CamCraft at c5bb09ed13f8b63e691d3a5ed6fb0be6a64ee2aa.

## What other tool libraries store

Fusion tool libraries store three kinds of mill that a `camcraft-tools` definition has no field for:

1. Form mill: a drawn profile, a list of (radius, height) points from the axis at the tip, round the cutter and back to the axis. It covers thread mills, double-angle cutters, radius-profile cutters and any ground shape.
2. Tapered mill: a cone with a tip diameter (flat) or a corner radius (ball) at the tip, a taper angle per side and a shoulder diameter at the cutting length (tapered engravers, ball-tip tapered mills).
3. Single-form thread mill: one tooth in the profile; Fusion states no pitch range (the range is in the description text, if anywhere).

## What is missing

- `kind: taper` is a cone from a sharp apex. A tool with a tip diameter or a ball tip has no field; writing it as `taper` shifts the cone by half the tip diameter at every height.
- The drawn cutter outline (`set_tool_cutter_profile`, `ToolCutter`) exists in a project but a `.camtools` definition cannot carry it (`tool_edit` lists `cutter` as not here), so an arbitrary form profile cannot travel with the tool. `kind: form` is a lathe gauge.
- `thread_mill_single` needs `pitch` and `pitch_min`; a source that stores only the tooth has neither.
- Smaller: the dovetail check `top < sr` compares with no tolerance, so a neck that meets the flank exactly (head 6.096 mm, 1.4605 mm high, 45 degree flank, neck 3.175 mm) is refused by float dust: `3.048 - 1.4605 / tan(45 deg)` is one ulp under `1.5875`.

## Synthetic example

Form mill, mm: profile `(0,0) (2,0) (4,0.8) (2,1.6) (2,9) (4,11) (4,40) (0,40)` (one 43.6 degree V tooth on a 4 mm radius shank).
Tapered mill, mm: tip diameter 1, taper angle 30 degrees per side, cutting length 10, shoulder diameter 12.

## Ask

Any of: a `tip_d` (and ball radius) on `taper`; an optional `cutter` outline in the definition, judged by `cutter_profile::check`; an optional `pitch_min` default for `thread_mill_single`; a small tolerance in the dovetail neck check.

Until then Dutchman writes only the multi-form thread mill (rows of equal teeth at one pitch, read from the profile) and the sharp-tipped taper, and reports the others as not carried over.

## Measured

On a 97-tool Fusion library: 85 written, 12 not written (11 single-tooth form mills, 1 tapered mill with a ball tip). One multi-form thread mill and one dovetail now convert.

body:
## What happens (CamCraft 0.25.0, Windows 11, release build, Intel integrated GPU, DX12)
Another process polled the window every 2 ms.
- The window is visible at about 40 ms (864x522) and resized at about 100 to 190 ms.
- It does not answer messages until about 730 to 1080 ms (3 runs, 5 MB project).
- Any SetWindowPos or ShowWindow call from another process blocks until then.
- With no project on the command line the freeze is the same length.

## Where the time goes
I added temporary timing lines (not in the patch). Milliseconds from `run_windowed`, release build:

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| Window created | 22 |
| GPU bring-up done | 226 |
| `StockEye::new` done | 658 |
| First frame start | 669 |
| Project loaded (5 MB) | 683 (14 ms) |
| First frame presented | 727 |

So the project load is not the cause. `StockEye::new` is about 430 ms. It compiles the composite and trace shaders. It runs on the UI thread before the first frame, but the eye is only used for the traced stock view. The browser shell already builds it after the first frame (`StockEye::new_async`).

## Patch (ready on a branch)
Build the eye on a worker thread (`shell_window/eye_boot.rs`). The shell takes it on a later frame. Until then the viewport draws the stock sheet. The eye syncs its sample count on its first frame (`apply_quality`).

Same probe, 3 runs each: first responsive at 730, 806 and 1079 ms before; 344, 369 and 448 ms after.

## Not fixed
About 300 ms remain: GPU bring-up (about 200 ms) and the first frame. Fixing it needs the bring-up off the UI thread, or the window created hidden and shown after the first frame. That is a larger design change. Which does the maintainer prefer?

Tests: unit tests for the hand-off (`eye_boot`). `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` passes (1479 tests) when it runs to the end. Not run: the gate tiers, clippy (not installed here), other platforms.

Separate note: on plain `main` (without this patch) the same test binary sometimes ends with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` at a random point (8 of 15 runs on Windows 11). The patch does not cause this. I can open a separate issue for it if wanted.

## What happens

ProfileCutout: 2D Contour, side outside, picked outer chain, entry plunge, stepdown 4.5, 4 tabs (width 10, height 3), bottom = bottom of model - 0.3, Router up-cut 6 mm. The untabbed levels (Z -4.5, -9, -13.5, -15.3) all lead in at the same point (X258.066 Y2.09), so each plunge is one stepdown into the kerf of the level above. G0 X242.068 Y1.89 Z25
```
G0 X246.667 Y90.812 Z25
G0 X246.667 Y90.812 Z2
G1 X246.667 Y90.812 Z-18 F600
G1 X253.739 Y87.072 Z-18 F1950
```

The upper levels cut along Y 88 there (kerf Y 85..91), so the Ø6 cutter centred at Y 90.812 (Y 87.8..93.8) plunges 18 mm with a 2.8 mm crescent of never-cut sheet beside it, at the plunge feed. Each tab hop then also feeds from Z -18 up to Z 12 and plunges 30 mm back down at F600 (lines 464-470 and on). The same happens on the Z -18.3 level. `verify` reports `ok: true`, no findings.

## Expected

Each level enters at most one stepdown below the floor the levels above left at the entry point (the same lead-in point as the untabbed levels, or a ramp), and tab hops rise only to the tab top plus a clearance.

[q07-router.camproj](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/q07-router.camproj), [q07-router.step](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/q07-router.step), posted [q07-router.nc](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/q07-router.nc) (operation ProfileCutout from line 372; the tabbed level at lines 456-490); agent report [REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/REPORT.md) problem 8.

| C300-C395 | BS2, 2nd cut |

Our post writes fixed condition numbers. The owner confirms that `C001` and `C002` **do** exist on his machine and are used for almost every pass, even though `COND.DAT` lists only `C100` and up. title: 2D Chamfer: select a tip offset

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Wanted

A 2D Chamfer can state a tip offset. The cone then cuts the requested chamfer through a radial band above that radius.

This lets the user keep the selected edge and the requested chamfer width. For example, a 6 mm chamfer mill can cut a 1 mm chamfer at a 2 mm tip offset. The cutting band is then 2 mm to 3 mm from the tool axis.

## Current behaviour

CamCraft places the virtual cone tip on the selected wall. It keeps the tip at:

```text
tip_z = top_z - width * tan(angle)
```

The tool centre has no XY offset from the picked line. A larger chamfer mill therefore cuts through the smallest part of its cone. The operation has no setting that moves to a larger-radius band of the same cone.

## Proposed rule

For an ideal sharp cone, add one operation value named `Tip offset`.

```text
tip offset = r
chamfer width = w
centreline offset toward air = r
tip_z = top_z - (r + w) * tan(chamfer angle)
contact radius = r to r + w
```

For a 45-degree chamfer, a 6 mm tool, `w = 1 mm`, and `r = 2 mm`:

```text
centreline offset = 2 mm
contact radius = 2 mm to 3 mm
tip_z = top_z - 3 mm
```

The final chamfer stays 1 mm wide. The tool uses a 2 mm to 3 mm part of the cone instead of its 0 mm to 1 mm part.

The `Side` setting determines the air side for closed rings and selected open chains.

## Safety doors

- Refuse when `r` is negative or not finite.
- Refuse when the tool radius is smaller than `r + width`.
- Refuse when the cone or flute reach cannot supply `(r + width) * tan(angle)`.
- Offset closed loops and open chains with the same air-side law.
- Refuse an offset that folds, disappears, or reaches material on the air side.
- Keep the declared `EdgeBreak` on the original picked edge with the authored width and depth. The larger contact band must not create credit for more edge work.
- Stock simulation and collision verification must judge the offset cone position, not the old tip-on-wall position.

## Scope

This issue does not model or compensate for tool-tip wear. It selects a band of the current ideal sharp cone.

Issue #895 is related because it tracks real flat, ball, and radiused tip geometry. This operation-level feature can be specified independently.

## Done means

- The Geometry page exposes `Tip offset` for a 2D Chamfer.
- The value round-trips through project files and the MCP operation parameter surface.
- A 45-degree, 6 mm ideal cone cuts an authored 1 mm chamfer with a 2 mm tip offset.
- A test proves the contact radii are 2 mm and 3 mm, and the tip path is 3 mm below the top plane.
- A motion test proves a closed ring offsets toward the side `Side` names.
- A motion test proves each selected open chain offsets toward its air side.
- The tool-radius and flute-reach refusals name the missing dimension.
- Stock simulation proves the final 1 mm edge break and no gouge on the part.
- Existing 0 mm tip offset projects keep the current path byte for byte.

## Labels

Suggested triage: `enhancement`, `area:2d`, `P6`, and `effort:high`.

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer can use a selected larger-radius band of a chamfer mill while preserving the authored chamfer width.

body:
Implement the core 4-axis cylindrical flow-line toolpath kernel in `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_flow.rs`.

What to build:
- Accept picked 3D guide edge chains, part facets, a rotary `Axis` (provided by the #2772 stated-axis resolver), `RotaryFlowParams`, and `AxisControl`.

- Parameterize the pair by normalized arc length, compute developed width `(s = R_ref * theta, v)`, and choose pass count from `stepover` or `scallop_stepover(r, tolerance)`.
- Adaptively chord each interpolated flow curve within `ARC_FIT_TOL` / `tolerance`.
- Compute gouge-free radial ball centers `rho_ball(theta, v)` where `min_tri dist(center, tri) >= r` via `closest_pt_tri`, so steep helical flanks never gouge.
- Link passes radially on the retract cylinder (matching `rotary_links`) and emit tool tips via `retip` and `command_axis`.

Provenance: published 4-axis cylindrical unwrapping and iso-parametric flow-line CAM literature; no vendor material consulted.

Depends on #2772 for stated rotary axis resolution on helical models.

Done means: `crates/motion::multiaxis::rotary_flow` generates gouge-free, radially posed passes across multi-turn helical bands on a rotor mesh in `crates/motion/tests/` and refuses invalid or single-chain inputs by name.

body:
Maintainer request from #1452 ("We should be able to load DXF file to do profile cuts on.").

Depends on #1860.

## Goal
Extend the `crates/geometry/src/dxf/` reader from #1860 to parse `SPLINE`, `ELLIPSE`, and bounded `BLOCK`/`INSERT` entities cleanly.

## Scope
- Parse `ELLIPSE` (center, major endpoint, axis ratio, start/end parameters, extrusion vector check) from Autodesk's published DXF Reference. Return exact `Circle`/`Arc` primitives when the axis ratio equals `1.0` within tolerance, and flatten non-circular ellipses adaptively within a caller chord tolerance in millimeters.
- Parse `SPLINE` (degree, flags, knot vector, control points, fit points, rational weights). Evaluate rational and non-rational B-splines via de Boor's algorithm and subdivide adaptively so chord deviation stays within the caller tolerance. Recover circular arcs when the spline matches a circle within tolerance. Reject malformed knot counts, negative weights, or non-finite control points by name.
- Pass the flattening chord tolerance through `ImportDxf` (#1862) and record it on import metadata.
- Parse `BLOCKS` definitions and expand `INSERT` references (translation, rotation, uniform X/Y scale, row/column array grids, and `0`-layer inheritance per DXF rules).
- Enforce strict recursion depth, total expanded entity count, and cycle detection caps against block bombs. Refuse cyclic references, external references (`XREF`), non-uniform X/Y shear scaling, or tilted OCS extrusions by block/entity name.

## Done means
Dense point sampling proves flattened `SPLINE` and `ELLIPSE` polylines stay within the stated tolerance in millimeters; circular splines and ellipses keep exact `Arc`/`Circle` segments; `INSERT` expands uniform blocks (and nested blocks within limits) accurately; cyclic blocks, sheared inserts, xrefs, and malformed splines return named errors with passing fuzz tests.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
